chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sakūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: “There are four upon whom there is no amputation: the snatcher, the one guilty of ghulūl, the one who steals from the war booty, and the theft of the hired worker, for it is treachery.”

key_terms.أَرْبَعَةٌ: four categories being identified in the ruling
key_terms.الْغَنِيمَةِ: war booty or spoils of war
key_terms.الْغُلُولُ: misappropriation or embezzlement, especially from shared or public spoils
key_terms.الْمُخْتَلِسُ: one who snatches property openly and quickly rather than committing qualifying secret theft
key_terms.قَطْعَ: the hadd punishment of amputation for theft

ai.seo_question: Which types of theft do not incur amputation in Shia hadith law?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the hadd punishment of amputation does not apply in four specific forms of taking property. It distinguishes technical theft that incurs hadd from acts classified instead as treachery or misappropriation within Islamic legal discourse.
